segments.text: Staying longer than six months? You have just one month to apply for this card in Spain.

It's called the TIE, the Foreigner Identity Card. If you hold a visa or a permit to stay in Spain for more than six months, getting it is both your right and your obligation. Whether you live in Madrid, Barcelona, Valencia, Seville or Malaga, it all starts on the same official website.

Now, the clock. For most long stays, like study, work or non-lucrative residence, your visa is only valid for ninety days. So whether you fly in from the United States, Mexico, Morocco or India, you must apply for your TIE within one month of entering Spain. And appointments can be weeks away.

Step one: book the appointment, the cita previa. Open the official website of Spain's public administration. Select your province of residence. Then choose the procedures of the National Police. Pick the option called Police, fingerprints, card issue. Finally, enter your details exactly as on your passport, choose an office and a time, and save your confirmation.

steps: Where you live, not where you landed
Print it or keep a screenshot

segments.text: Your province decides where you go. Someone living in Alicante books in Alicante. In Palma, on the island of Mallorca, you book in the Balearic Islands. In Las Palmas, on Gran Canaria, you book in the Canary Islands. Always pick the province where you live, not the city where you landed.

Step two: get your documents ready. First, the application form, called EX seventeen. Second, proof that you paid the fee, with form seven ninety, code zero twelve. Third, your valid passport, plus a photocopy. And fourth, one recent colour photo that meets the rules for Spanish ID cards. Missing one can cost you the appointment.

How much does it cost? For a first card that documents a temporary residence or stay, the official fee is sixteen euros and eight cents. A renewal card costs nineteen euros and thirty cents. You fill in form seven ninety online, on the National Police website, and pay it before your appointment in Madrid or anywhere else.

Step three: appointment day. Go to the police office you booked, whether that's in Madrid, Zaragoza, Bilbao, Barcelona or Seville. Arrive on time, with every document in your hand. An officer checks your papers and takes your fingerprints. That's why everyone calls it the fingerprint appointment, or toma de huellas.

Three smart tips. One: book as early as you can, because the wait can be several weeks. Two: if the immigration office already sent you a positive resolution, it is valid while you wait for the card. Three: only book on the official government website, and keep copies of everything you hand in.

Already living here and renewing? Once your renewal is approved, you need a new card too, with the same booking, the same form and the renewal fee. The steps are identical in Granada, Murcia and Valladolid. And your card stays valid for as long as your residence permit does.

Let's recap. Book your cita previa on the official site. Choose your province and the fingerprint option. Bring form EX seventeen, the fee receipt, your passport and a photo. Then show up, give your fingerprints, and your TIE is on its way.

Rules can change, so always check the official site before you go. Which step confused you the most? Tell us in the comments. Next, watch our video on Spain itself, and subscribe to join us for the next country.
